children: WALL STREET STOCKS FINISH LOWER AS RISING CRUDE PRICES WEAKEN SENTIMENT
U.S. stocks closed lower on Monday as rising crude prices, following a renewed escalation of hostilities in the Middle East, weighed on investor sentiment.

Investors were also assessing what was seen as a hawkish message from Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell at the Jackson Hole symposium on Friday, where he reaffirmed the central bank's commitment to its inflation target, pushing U.S. Treasury yields higher.
Traders are pricing in a 66% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate increase in September, according to CME's FedWatch tool.
Most S&P 500 sectors ended the session in negative territory. Take-Two Interactive
shares fell 6.7%, making the videogame publisher the biggest percentage decliner and one of the biggest drags on the communication services sector
led sector gains, followed by technology shares
rose 5.5% for its biggest percentage gain since July 6. It was the second biggest boost to the S&P 500 behind Nvidia
Here is the closing market snapshot:
Wall Street indexes dip; Dow leads losses, off 0.70%
Comms svcs leads S&P 500 sector losses, energy and technology rise
Dollar dips, US crude up >2%, gold slips ~0.1%, bitcoin rises
